newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Smithkline reined in by stronger pound.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Smithkline reined in by stronger pound.

text.p: Drugs giant SmithKline Beecham Plc said on Tuesday that the surging pound muffled an otherwise strong rise in first-quarter profits.

Underlining the challenge to British-based companies, the Anglo-U.S. group said sterling's rise against other European currencies and the dollar wiped 41 million pounds ($66.9 million) off profits in the first three months of the year.
Pre-tax profits rose 8 percent to 418 million pounds, while sales actually fell by two percent to 1.84 billion pounds. The dividend rose by 10.3 percent to 4.41 pence per share.
At constant exchange rates the company said its pre-tax profit would have been ahead by 19 percent to 459 million pounds.
However investors took the bad news on currency in their stride, pushing SmithKline's shares up 28 pence to close at 934 pence a share.

SmithKline Beecham, which is the world's ninth biggest prescription drugs group in terms of market share, again pointed to a robust performance by products launched over the past five years as a sign of its rude good health.
Sales of new drugs jumped by 40 percent to 354 million pounds in the first quarter, led by rapid growth in Seroxat/Paxil, an anti-depressant rival to Eli Lilly & Co's blockbuster Prozac.

Sales of Seroxat/Paxil climbed 49 percent to 197 million pounds in the three months to March, putting it in a race with anti-biotic Augmentin to be the group's biggest seller. Augmentin sales rose 29 percent to 255 million pounds.
"The underlying growth is excellent, principally through new products, and we are getting good growth both in pharmaceuticals and consumer healthcare," finance director Hugh Collum told Reuters.

There was disappointment among analysts however at the 12 percent underlying rise in drugs sales, which SocGen's Paul Diggle said put it behind its U.S. peer group. He said that so far only Sweden's Astra AB and Switzerland's Roche Holding AG had posted lower first-quarter drug sales growth.

However consumer healthcare, which includes a string of household names such as Aquafresh toothpaste, Lucozade and Panadol, put in a robust performance with sales excluding currency ahead 18 percent to 549 million pounds and operating profits up 20 percent.

The company's U.S. Clinical Laboratories operations continued to limp along amid strong competition for its hospital testing services, with profits dropping 25 percent to 12 million pounds excluding currency.

Despite the problems and recent controversy over alleged pricing irregularities, which saw SmithKline agree to pay its biggest customer the U.S. government $325 million in February, Collum told Reuters there were no plans to divest the business.

SocGen's Diggle said the results "were fine but not enough to excite very much," adding that SmithKline was on target to achieve his forecast of 11 percent growth in full-year pre-tax profit to 1.73 billion pounds.

"It will probably be the best quarter in terms of underlying growth but it will also be the worst for currency, so I think we will keep with our view for the year," he added. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
